chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man committed an offense against me; should I pardon him, or should I bring him before the authority? He said: “It is your right. If you pardon him, that is good; and if you bring him to the Imam, then you have only sought your right. But how can you reach the Imam?”

key_terms.السُّلْطَانِ: the ruling authority to whom a grievance may be brought
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam as the legitimate authority for judgment

ai.seo_question: Can a person forgive an offender instead of taking the case to the Imam or ruler?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the wronged person has the right either to pardon the offender or to seek redress through the Imam. It presents forgiveness as good, while also affirming the legitimacy of pursuing one’s lawful right through proper authority.
